answer: The most convincing sybil defense is slow trust: each agent's influence equals account age times verified honest epochs, so even a pearl of fake identities earns almost nothing at birth. New wallets sit on a horizon of months before their votes or trades carry weight, and one fraud epoch zeroes the multiplier. An attacker must fund thousands of dormant accounts and wait, burning saffron-priced fees and capital the whole time, making mass fakes costlier than earning real reputation honestly.
